topics.title: Norway gets a new king
topics.summary: Norway's King Harald V died at 89, and his son became King Haakon VIII, beginning a new chapter for one of Europe's longstanding monarchies.
topics.discussionPrompt: If your family suddenly inherited a ceremonial job, who would take it way too seriously and who would redesign the uniform first?

topics.title: Lake Ontario rename stirs chatter
topics.summary: President Trump signed an order renaming Lake Ontario as Lake America within the United States, setting up new questions about maps, signage and cross-border reaction.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a famous local landmark got renamed overnight, what nickname would actually stick around the studio?

topics.title: Fed weighs inflation pressure
topics.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said interest rate hikes remain possible if inflation stays stubborn, keeping households and markets watching the next economic signals closely.
topics.discussionPrompt: What would the studio cut from its budget first if borrowing suddenly got pricier: props, snacks, or someone’s extremely specific coffee order?

topics.title: Mortgage rates climb again
topics.summary: The average U.S. 30-year mortgage rate rose to 6.66%, returning near levels seen four weeks ago and adding pressure to an already tight housing market.
topics.discussionPrompt: If everyone had to share one dream house, what room would cause the first negotiation meltdown?

topics.title: Tropical storms gather attention
topics.summary: Forecasters tracked Tropical Storms Karina and Lowell in the Pacific while Dolly churned in the Atlantic, adding another busy watch point to hurricane season.
topics.discussionPrompt: Who in the studio would overprepare for storm season, and who would still forget batteries until the last possible minute?

topics.title: PGA sponsor shakeup lands
topics.summary: Golf brand Good Good will no longer be the title sponsor of a PGA Tour event and also lost its Callaway sponsorship, shifting a high-profile sports partnership.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the studio had a sponsor, what product would be hilarious, useful, or immediately suspicious?

topics.title: Lunar eclipse lights skies
topics.summary: A lunar eclipse lit up skies across the Americas and Europe, giving photographers and sky watchers a dramatic night show from many different viewpoints.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would the characters plan a calm eclipse watch party, or accidentally turn it into a competition over who understands the moon best?

topics.title: Night owl habits studied
topics.summary: Health researchers highlighted links between late-night routines and heart risks, while noting that sleep timing and habits can often be adjusted gradually.
topics.discussionPrompt: Who is secretly most functional after midnight, and who becomes dramatic if bedtime moves by five minutes?

topics.title: Pancreatic cancer pill approved
topics.summary: The FDA approved Revolution Medicines' daily pills for a form of pancreatic cancer, a notable treatment milestone for a disease with limited options.
topics.discussionPrompt: How would the studio celebrate a genuine medical breakthrough without turning the whole room awkwardly sentimental?

topics.title: Red Solo cup gets its moment
topics.summary: AP looked at the red Solo cup's place in American party culture, from casual gatherings to its instantly recognizable role in pop culture.
topics.discussionPrompt: What ordinary object in the studio deserves a suspiciously serious documentary treatment?
